# Microfinance and SACCO Lending Policy

This policy governs group and individual lending activity conducted through the Savings and Credit Cooperative (SACCO) channel, covering loan products, member eligibility, group guarantee mechanics, and default handling procedures for the microfinance portfolio.

## Loan Products and Eligibility

The SACCO offers three loan products to its members: a short-term working-capital loan repayable within six months, a school-fees loan disbursed twice yearly ahead of each academic term, and an asset-financing loan for income-generating equipment repayable over up to eighteen months. A member becomes eligible for any loan product only after maintaining active savings contributions for a minimum of three consecutive months and holding no outstanding arrears on a prior SACCO obligation.

## Group Guarantee and Solidarity Lending

Loans disbursed through a lending group of five to fifteen members rely on a solidarity guarantee, under which every group member is jointly liable for the full outstanding balance of any single member's loan. Group formation must be approved by a SACCO field officer, who confirms that members reside within the same operating area and do not already belong to another active lending group, to prevent overlapping guarantee exposure.

## Interest Rates and Fee Structure

All loan products carry a flat monthly interest rate set by the SACCO board and published in the member handbook, together with a one-time processing fee deducted from the disbursed principal. Interest rates may be revised no more than once per calendar year, and any revision takes effect only for loans disbursed after the revision date, never retroactively on existing balances.

## Default and Arrears Management

A loan is classified as in arrears once a scheduled repayment is more than fifteen days overdue, triggering a first-contact visit from the assigned field officer. If the arrears persist beyond sixty days, the group guarantee is invoked and the remaining group members become responsible for covering the shortfall from their own savings balances or subsequent group contributions.

## Governance and Board Oversight

The SACCO board reviews the aggregate loan portfolio at each monthly meeting, focusing on the portfolio-at-risk ratio, the performance of individual lending groups, and any proposed changes to loan products or eligibility criteria. Any change to this policy requires a two-thirds majority vote of the board and must be communicated to all field officers before taking effect.
